name: Cuban Press
description: The Cuban press is a three-phase shoulder exercise that combines an upright row, external rotation, and an overhead press in a single movement. It trains the full rotator cuff through a functional arc, particularly emphasizing the external rotators and infraspinatus. Originally developed for overhead athletes requiring rotator cuff health and shoulder mobility, the Cuban press is used both as a corrective exercise and as a warm-up for heavy overhead pressing sessions.

execution.starting_position: Stand holding dumbbells (or a barbell) at thigh level with an overhand grip.
execution.setup_instructions: Use very light weights — this is a technique and health exercise, not a strength movement. 2.5-10 lbs per dumbbell is typical.
steps: Step 1: Begin with dumbbells at the thighs.
Step 2: Upright row phase: raise the elbows up and out to bring the weights to shoulder height with elbows at 90 degrees and upper arms parallel to the floor.
Step 3: External rotation phase: rotate the forearms upward until forearms are vertical (elbows still at 90 degrees, now pointing up).
Step 4: Press phase: press the dumbbells overhead to full lockout.
Step 5: Reverse the motion through each phase back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe naturally — this is typically used for warm-up or corrective purposes.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight, which corrupts the rotation technique
Skipping the controlled return through all three phases
Rushing through the exercise without pausing at each transition
safety_considerations: This exercise should feel comfortable — any shoulder pain is a signal to stop and assess
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full upright row height, full external rotation, full overhead lockout — three distinct positions.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Slow and deliberate through each phase — no specific tempo beyond controlled execution
coaching_cues: Three distinct movements — row, rotate, press
Light weight — quality of motion matters
Reverse every phase on the way down
